what_it_is: Lane discipline: the mechanical rules that keep twelve workers from colliding, stalling, or silently losing work. One worker per lane. Claim-liveness auditing every tick: no sign-in naming the brief after 2 ticks → the brief returns to the queue; sign-in with no receipt after 6 ticks → STALE. Rotation-queued entries verified on disk.
what_it_does: Prevents the three lane failure modes: races (two seats on the same work), ghosts (claims with no worker behind them), and squatting (a claim held with no heartbeat). The claim-liveness audit is the tripwire — every handoff state has one.
why_it_matters: The #2533 scorecard brief — the single merge blocker for milestone 1 — sat in claimed/ for 18+ minutes with no lane-feed sign-in while the rotation still listed it queued. The queue had silently lost the critical-path brief and no job watched claimed/. The fix was mechanical: void the phantom claim, return it to the queue, and wire the claim-liveness audit into the dispatcher (THE PHANTOM-CLAIM LAW, 2026-10-13). A claim without a sign-in is a reservation without a worker.
key_rules: One worker per lane, one claim per worker, sign-in as the proof of life.
The cycle, in order: claim → sign-in → read → work → receipt → release. No exceptions.
A claim without a sign-in after 2 ticks returns to the queue (phantom claim). A sign-in with no receipt after 6 ticks goes STALE.
Take the OLDEST unclaimed brief — oldest-first pickup. Never claim from memory.
First claim stands: on collision, the later seat renumbers or stands down — never overwrites.
Dispatch only to free lanes. A rank that can't be executed is a wish list.
Enforcement must check BOTH sign-in feeds (main lane-feed.md and brief-queue/lane-feed.md) — a healthy claim dies if the audit looks in only one place.
test: Did I post a sign-in BEFORE reading the brief — claim → sign-in → read, in that exact order, no exceptions?
Does my sign-in name the lane, the tick, the claimed brief's filename, and one task line?
Is my claim still fresh (receipt within 6 ticks), or am I squatting on a lane with no heartbeat?
Did I check that no other seat holds this brief, lane, or work item before I claimed it?
If I collide with another seat's claim, does the first claim stand — and do I renumber / stand down, not overwrite?
If the claim-liveness audit ran this tick, would my claim survive — sign-in matched, inside the window?
When I finish or stall, will the lane release cleanly — brief to done/ (or stale/), receipt posted, sign-out on the feed?

enforcement.real: Claim-liveness audit in the night-dispatcher, every tick: claimed/ grepped against sign-ins — no sign-in after 2 ticks → back to queue + log + lesson; sign-in with no receipt after 6 ticks → STALE; rotation-queued entries verified on disk. violation-detector-class17.py (sha 085f592e): 8 admission patterns, 28/28 live catch, 0 false positives. Dispatcher-side free-lane check: dispatch only to free lanes — 'one worker per lane' enforced at dispatch time, not just claim time.
